sentence: This project brings together scientists to promote progress in the biology of dendritic cells, which help the body build immunity to infections.
This project tests which treatment best rescues vision in a mouse model of a severe disease and studies why retinal ganglion cells are lost.
This project studies how stress in the environment affects the risk of Alzheimer's disease by comparing people living in cities and in rural areas.
This project studies how metastatic cancer cells change their gene expression to adapt to stress, using patient samples and organoids.
This project studies how heart damage from cancer therapies differs among breast cancer survivors and uses machine learning to predict risk.
This project uses brain imaging to compare kappa opioid receptors in people with opioid use disorder and healthy controls.
This project studies how an enzyme in immune cells leads to heart problems in Takotsubo cardiomyopathy and raises later cardiovascular risk.
This project develops neural interfaces and other technologies that help people with limb loss or sensorimotor impairments move and stay healthy.
This project studies how gene expression is changed in the placentas of people with Down syndrome and why these placentas develop defects.
This project studies how HIV persists in cytotoxic T cells, using single-cell profiling of how they respond to antigens and cytokines.
This project builds computational algorithms that find patterns in data to predict how infections with two organisms become life-threatening.
This project studies how chimeric mRNA makes gasdermin fusion proteins that control inflammatory cell death and shape the immune response.
This project builds imaging methods using mass spectrometry and magnetic resonance to map metabolites across cells and tissues over time.
This project uses computational methods to study changes in metabolism in children with Crohn's disease and to predict who will develop severe disease.
This project studies how the transcription cycle and RNA polymerase work in Mycobacterium tuberculosis and related bacteria.
This project builds a tool that uses machine learning on images to measure head shape differences in craniosynostosis and help physicians and researchers.
This project tests small molecules that block an immunosuppressive pathway to reverse immune suppression in glioblastoma.
This project builds digital twins of lymph nodes using machine learning to study how inflammation changes drug penetration during HIV infection.
This project builds a machine learning dosing system that uses lifestyle, clinical and pharmacogenomic data to guide warfarin doses for patients.
This project engineers realistic tissues and mini-organs from natural collagen to study how physical signals from the matrix drive changes in cells.
